name: Prednisone
route_note: oral tablet or solution, usually once daily in the morning; delayed-release tablet (Rayos) at night

discovery.note: Produced by microbial 1,2-dehydrogenation of cortisone with Corynebacterium simplex.

tagline: The everyday oral steroid, converted by the liver into prednisolone
summary: Prednisone is a synthetic glucocorticoid that is inactive until converted to prednisolone in the liver. It is about four times as potent as hydrocortisone with less salt retention, and is one of the most widely used oral anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive drugs, especially in North America.
mechanism: Prednisone is a prodrug: 11β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 1 in the liver reduces its 11-keto group to the 11β-hydroxyl of prednisolone, the active compound.

Glucocorticoids diffuse into cells and bind the cytoplasmic glucocorticoid receptor (NR3C1). The activated receptor moves to the nucleus, where it switches on anti-inflammatory genes (transactivation, e.g. annexin-1, IκBα, MKP-1) and represses pro-inflammatory transcription factors such as NF-κB and AP-1 (transrepression), reducing cytokines, prostaglandins, adhesion molecules and immune-cell activation.
uses: Rheumatic diseases (rheumatoid arthritis, polymyalgia rheumatica, vasculitis, lupus)
Haematological cancers in combination regimens (e.g. lymphoma, myeloma)

history.title: Cortisone in arthritis
history.detail: Philip Hench's use of cortisone in rheumatoid arthritis launches corticosteroid therapy.

history.title: Nobel Prize
history.detail: Kendall, Hench and Reichstein receive the Nobel Prize for adrenal cortex hormones.

history.title: Microbial dehydrogenation
history.detail: Schering's Arthur Nobile converts cortisone into prednisone using bacteria.

history.title: Approval
history.detail: Prednisone is approved and marketed as Meticorten, greatly reducing salt-retaining side effects of earlier steroids.

history.title: Delayed-release tablet
history.detail: FDA approves Rayos, a delayed-release prednisone taken at bedtime for rheumatoid arthritis.

pk.metabolism: hepatic conversion to prednisolone, then further metabolism

serious: adrenal suppression and adrenal crisis on abrupt withdrawal

facts: Prednisone is preferred in the US while prednisolone is preferred in the UK and much of Europe.
Both prednisone and prednisolone were introduced by Schering in 1955.
